en: to apply for; to file an application for

examples.en: We filed the new technology as a patent.
I'm going to file the company name as a trademark.
It's safer to file this idea first.
I heard he filed applications for as many as three inventions.
Sir, when did you file for that design?
After you file, you have to wait for the examination.

explain: '특허를 출원하다', '상표를 출원하다'처럼 권리를 신청할 때 써요. 입학이나 취업은 '출원'이 아니라 '지원하다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 우리 팀은 새 기술로 특허를 출원했어요.
phrases.en: Our team filed a patent for the new technology.
phrases.nuance_ko: '출원하다'와 가장 자주 함께 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation with '출원하다'.

phrases.en: I'm planning to file the design next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 신청할 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state an upcoming plan to apply.

phrases.en: The documents were incomplete, so I haven't been able to file yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 할 수 없었던 상황을 부정형으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form for a situation where filing wasn't possible.

explain_en: Formal legal filing, mainly patents or trademarks. It is used for applying for rights, as in '특허를 출원하다' and '상표를 출원하다'. For admissions or jobs, use '지원하다' instead, not '출원하다'.

t90.ax: It's safer to file this idea first.

examples.en: The uncle got his nephew a job at his company.

examples.ko: 부모님은 아들을 빨리 취직시키고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: The parents want to get their son a job quickly.

examples.ko: 선배가 저를 아는 회사에 취직시켜 줬어요.
examples.en: A senior got me a job at a company he knows.
The father tried hard to get his daughter a job at a bank.
I thanked the boss who gave my friend a job.

examples.ko: 그 사람을 취직시킬 방법이 없어서 고민이에요.
examples.en: I am worried because there is no way to get that person a job.

explain: 'A가 B를 회사에 취직시키다'처럼 일하게 해 주는 사람과 일자리를 얻는 사람이 따로 있어요. 내가 일자리를 얻는 건 '취직하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The senior got his junior a job at the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남이 일자리를 얻도록 도와줄 때 '-아/어 주다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -아/어 주다 when someone helps another person get a job.

phrases.en: My friend asked me to get him a job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일자리를 구해 달라고 부탁하는 상황에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone asks you to find them a job.
phrases.en_equiv: to ask someone to get a job for them

phrases.en: The boss is going to get his nephew a job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 그렇게 하겠다는 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say what someone plans to do.

explain_en: Causative; one person arranges a job for another, often through connections. In 'A가 B를 회사에 취직시키다', the person who arranges the job and the person who gets it are different. When you get a job yourself, use '취직하다'.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 코미디언이 되고 싶었어요.
examples.en: I wanted to be a comedian since I was little.
That comedian makes people laugh with just his expression.
I saw a famous comedian on TV yesterday.

examples.ko: 코미디언 친구가 생일 파티에서 노래를 불렀어요.
examples.en: My comedian friend sang a song at the birthday party.
If you talk like a comedian, the mood loosens up quickly.

examples.ko: 우리 반에는 코미디언 같은 학생이 한 명 있어요.
examples.en: There is one student in our class who is like a comedian.

explain: 방송에서는 '개그맨', '개그우먼'이라는 말을 더 자주 써요. 코미디언은 성별과 상관없이 쓸 수 있어서 소개할 때 안전한 말이에요. 재미있는 친구에게는 보통 '웃긴 사람'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: That comedian often appears on TV.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방송에서 많이 쓰는 말이고, 보통 남자 코미디언을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in broadcasting and usually refers to a male comedian.

phrases.en: I saw a famous comedian in person.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유명한'을 앞에 붙여 사람을 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 유명한 before it to introduce a person.

phrases.en: My younger sibling talks in a funny way like a comedian.
phrases.nuance_ko: 웃긴 사람을 비유할 때 '처럼'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 처럼 to compare a funny person to a comedian.

explain_en: On Korean TV people often say 개그맨 and 개그우먼. 코미디언 works for any gender, so it is a safe word when you introduce someone. For a funny friend, people usually just say 웃긴 사람.

t90.ax: I saw a famous comedian on TV yesterday.

examples.en: My uncle works as a programmer at a big company.
The programmer made a new app.
I have dreamed of being a programmer since I was young.
Programmers often work at night.
The programmer's desk is full of coffee.
The programmer and the designer hold a meeting together.

explain: 회사에서는 '개발자'라는 말도 자주 써요. 두 말을 거의 같은 사람에게 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 직업을 말할 때는 '프로그래머로 일하다'처럼 '로'를 붙여요.

phrases.en: My older brother is a developer who makes apps.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거의 같은 사람에게 쓰는 말이에요. 회사에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for almost the same people; common at companies.

phrases.en: My older sister works as a programmer at a game company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업을 말할 때 '로'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '로' when stating a job.

phrases.en: I study to become a programmer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 목표를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about a dream or goal.

explain_en: Companies also use the word '개발자' (developer), and the two often refer to the same people. When naming the job, add '로', as in '프로그래머로 일하다'.

examples.en: The principal greeted the students at the graduation ceremony.
I wrote a letter addressed to the principal.

examples.ko: 우리 학교장은 아침마다 정문에서 학생들을 맞아요.
examples.en: Our principal greets students at the front gate every morning.

examples.ko: 학교장의 허락을 받아야 행사를 열 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can hold the event only with the principal's permission.
There was a time to introduce the new principal.

examples.ko: 학교장 추천서가 있어야 지원할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can apply only with a letter of recommendation from the principal.

explain: 말할 때는 '교장 선생님'이라고 부르고, '학교장'은 공문, 서류, 뉴스에서 주로 써요. '학교장 추천', '학교장 허가'처럼 제도 이름에 많이 나와요. 학교 안에서 직접 부를 때는 꼭 '교장 선생님'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I received a scholarship through the principal's recommendation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제도나 서류에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often seen in systems and official documents.

phrases.example: 현장 체험을 가려면 학교장 허가가 필요해요.
phrases.en: You need the principal's permission to go on a field trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교에서 공식적으로 허락받는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when official permission is needed at school.

phrases.en: The principal greeted the students.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말로 부르거나 이야기할 때는 이 말을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is what you use when speaking to or about the principal.

explain_en: In speech people say '교장 선생님'; '학교장' is mostly for official letters, documents, and news. It often appears in system names like '학교장 추천' and '학교장 허가'. At school, address the person as '교장 선생님'.

examples.en: I studied Korean in my undergraduate program.

examples.ko: 학부 때는 친구들과 동아리 활동을 많이 했어요.
examples.en: In my undergraduate years, I did a lot of club activities with friends.

examples.ko: 학부를 졸업한 뒤에 대학원에 갈 거예요.
examples.en: After finishing my undergraduate degree, I'll go to graduate school.

examples.ko: 학부생이라서 아직 연구실에 들어갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: I'm an undergraduate, so I can't join a research lab yet.

examples.ko: 이 대학교는 학부마다 건물이 따로 있어요.
examples.en: At this university, each college has its own building.
My younger sibling enters the undergraduate program this year.

explain: 한국 대학에서 '학부'는 대학교 4년 과정을 말하고, 그 위 과정은 '대학원'이에요. '경영학부'처럼 학과보다 큰 단위의 이름에도 써요. 학부에 다니는 학생은 '학부생'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I'm a third-year undergraduate student.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학부에 다니는 학생을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a student enrolled in an undergraduate program.

phrases.en: My major as an undergraduate was business.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학원생이나 졸업한 사람이 대학교 시절을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used by graduate students or graduates to refer to their college years.

phrases.en: The undergraduate program usually takes four years.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대학원 과정'과 구별해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to distinguish from the graduate school program.

explain_en: In a Korean university, '학부' is the undergraduate program, and the level above it is '대학원' (graduate school). It's also used in names of divisions larger than a department, like '경영학부'. A student in it is a '학부생'.

examples.en: He works as a mate on a large ship.

examples.ko: 항해사는 배가 가는 길을 정하고 지도를 봐요.
examples.en: A ship's navigator decides the route and reads the charts.
My father sailed the seas as a ship's officer for twenty years.

examples.ko: 항해사가 되려면 해양 대학에서 공부해야 해요.
examples.en: To become a ship's officer, you have to study at a maritime university.

examples.ko: 선장과 항해사가 날씨를 보고 이야기하고 있어요.
examples.en: The captain and the mate are talking while looking at the weather.

examples.ko: 신입 항해사에게 배 운항 방법을 가르쳐 줬어요.
examples.en: They taught the new mate how to operate the ship.

explain: 선장을 도와 배가 갈 길을 정하고 배를 모는 일을 맡은 선원이에요. 배 전체를 책임지는 사람은 '선장'이고, 엔진을 맡는 사람은 '기관사'라고 해요.

phrases.en: He was promoted to first mate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선장 다음으로 높은 항해사를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the highest-ranking mate after the captain.

phrases.en: I've wanted to become a ship's navigator since I was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 직업을 말할 때 쓰는 기본 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A basic form for talking about dreams or jobs.

phrases.en: I'm studying hard to get a navigator's license.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이 직업에 필요한 자격을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the qualification needed for this job.

explain_en: This is the crew member who helps the captain plan the route and steer the ship. The person responsible for the whole ship is the '선장' (captain), and the one in charge of the engines is the '기관사' (engineer).

en: being active; being current; being incumbent

examples.ko: 그 선수는 마흔 살인데도 아직 현역이에요.
examples.en: That player is forty but still active.
My father went to the army on active duty.

examples.ko: 현역 의원들이 오늘 모여서 회의를 했어요.
examples.en: The sitting lawmakers met today for a meeting.

examples.ko: 은퇴한 가수가 현역 시절 노래를 다시 불렀어요.
examples.en: The retired singer sang a song from the days of his career again.

examples.ko: 삼촌은 현역에서 물러나 지금은 감독을 해요.
examples.en: My uncle retired from active play and now works as a coach.

examples.ko: 저 배우는 지금도 현역으로 활동하고 있어요.
examples.en: That actor is still working actively today.

explain: 현역은 지금도 그 일을 하고 있는 사람을 말할 때 써요. 반대말은 '은퇴'예요. 군대에서는 '현역'과 '예비역'을 나눠서 말해요.

phrases.en: Active players gathered at the stadium.
phrases.nuance_ko: 은퇴하지 않고 아직 뛰는 선수를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Players who haven't retired and still play.

phrases.en: That singer retired from active work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말인 '은퇴'와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used together with its opposite, 은퇴.

phrases.en: My uncle is an active-duty soldier.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군대에서 지금 복무하는 사람이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person currently serving in the military.

explain_en: Person still active in a job, sport or military. 현역 is used for someone who is still working in a field, in sports, politics or the military. The opposite is 은퇴 (retirement). In the army, 현역 (active) is separate from 예비역 (reserves).

examples.en: My successor starts work next week.
The team leader has not found a replacement yet.
I taught my successor the job step by step.
I heard the successor is someone with a lot of experience.

examples.ko: 퇴사하기 전에 후임자와 함께 일을 정리했어요.
examples.en: Before leaving the company, I sorted out the work together with my successor.

examples.ko: 후임자로 뽑힌 사람은 저와 같은 학교 출신이에요.
examples.en: The person chosen as my successor graduated from the same school as me.

explain: 회사에서 내 일을 이어받는 사람은 '후임자', 앞서 맡았던 사람은 '전임자'예요. 보통 '후임자를 구하다', '후임자로 정해지다'처럼 써요. 군대에서는 나보다 늦게 들어온 사람을 줄여서 '후임'이라고 많이 불러요.

phrases.en: The company is selecting a successor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 사람을 고를 때 써요. 채용 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when choosing a new person. Often comes up in talk about hiring.

phrases.en: I was chosen as Manager Kim's successor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누구의 자리를 이어받는지 말할 때 써요. '-의 후임자'로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say whose position you take over. Said as '-의 후임자'.

phrases.en: I handed my work over to my successor well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일을 이어받을 사람에게 전해 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when passing work on to the person taking over.

explain_en: The person who takes over the work, handover context (후임자에게 설명) The person who takes over your work is the 후임자, and the one who held the post before is the 전임자. It is used as '후임자를 구하다' (find a successor) or '후임자로 정해지다' (be chosen as successor). In the military, someone who joined after you is often called simply '후임'.

t90.ax: My successor starts work next week.

examples.en: There is a famous orchestra in our city.

examples.ko: 관현악단 연주회 표를 두 장 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought two tickets for the orchestra concert.

examples.ko: 그 관현악단은 매년 해외 공연을 가요.
examples.en: That orchestra goes on overseas tours every year.
My younger sibling plays the violin in the school orchestra.
The orchestra and the choir went on stage together.
The conductor entered leading the orchestra.

explain: 현악기, 관악기, 타악기가 함께 연주하는 단체를 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '오케스트라'라고 많이 하고, '관현악단'은 공연 안내나 뉴스 같은 격식 있는 글에서 볼 수 있어요. '교향악단'도 비슷하게 쓰여요.

phrases.en: I play the violin in the school orchestra.
phrases.nuance_ko: 관현악단보다 일상 대화에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common than 관현악단 in everyday talk.

phrases.en: I saw a Seoul symphony orchestra concert on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 관현악단과 비슷하게 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal word used much like 관현악단.

phrases.example: 시립 관현악단이 공원에서 무료 공연을 해요.
phrases.en: The city orchestra gives a free concert in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도시에서 운영하는 관현악단을 말할 때 앞에 '시립'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 시립 in front for an orchestra run by a city.

explain_en: Formal, Sino-Korean — used in official group names and writing. It means a group in which string, wind and percussion instruments play together. In daily talk people often say '오케스트라', while '관현악단' appears in concert notices and news, which are more formal. '교향악단' is used in a similar way.

t90.ax: There is a famous orchestra in our city.

examples.en: That athlete is an Olympic gold medalist.
A gold medalist came to our school and gave a talk.
I took a photo with a gold medalist.
I heard even gold medalists were ordinary kids at first.
A gold medalist's daily training is really long.

examples.ko: 이번 대회 금메달리스트에게 큰 박수를 보냈어요.
examples.en: We gave a big round of applause to this tournament's gold medalist.

explain: '금메달리스트'는 외래어 '메달리스트'에 '금'이 붙은 말이에요. 은메달은 '은메달리스트', 동메달은 '동메달리스트'로 이어서 써요. '금메달을 따다'로 말하고 '금메달을 받다'도 가능해요.

phrases.en: I want to become a gold medalist someday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 목표를 말할 때 '되다'와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with 되다 when talking about dreams or goals.

phrases.en: Our athlete won a gold medal in swimming.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 대신 메달 자체를 말해서 경기 결과를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Talks about the medal itself rather than the person, to describe a result.

phrases.en: My father met an Olympic gold medalist in person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에 대회 이름을 붙이면 어느 대회에서 우승했는지 알 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding the name of the event tells which competition the person won.

explain_en: 금메달리스트 is 금 plus the loanword 메달리스트. Silver and bronze follow the same pattern: 은메달리스트 and 동메달리스트. The usual verb is 금메달을 따다, and 금메달을 받다 also works.

examples.en: At first, that actor only played minor roles.
I appeared briefly in a drama as a bit player.
Even if it's a minor role, I want to act hard.
I heard my friend appeared in a movie in a small part.
Even the bit-part actors gather early at the set.
She started with minor roles and worked up to the lead.

explain: '주연', '조연'과 나란히 나오는 말인데, 단역은 대사가 거의 없거나 잠깐 나오는 역이에요. '단역 배우', '단역을 맡다'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 그는 단역 배우로 십 년 동안 일했어요.
phrases.en: He worked as a bit-part actor for ten years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 역을 맡는 배우를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an actor who plays small roles.

phrases.en: I took a minor role in the school play.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 역할을 하게 되었다고 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The usual pairing for being given a small part.

phrases.en: My friend appeared in the movie in a small role.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잠깐 화면에 보이는 역할로 출연했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means appearing briefly on screen in a small part.
phrases.en_equiv: to appear in a minor role

explain_en: It sits alongside '주연' (lead) and '조연' (supporting), but a 단역 is a role with few or no lines or only a brief appearance. You say '단역 배우' or '단역을 맡다'.

examples.en: I go to learn pottery every weekend.
I made a cup myself in pottery class.
I became interested in pottery, so I signed up at a workshop.

examples.ko: 이 도예 작품은 색이 정말 독특해요.
examples.en: The color of this pottery piece is really unique.

examples.ko: 도예로 만든 그릇은 하나하나 모양이 달라요.
examples.en: Each bowl made by pottery has a different shape.
My friend gave me a pottery experience class as a gift.

explain: 만든 물건은 '도자기', 만드는 일이나 분야는 '도예'라고 해요. '도예 수업', '도예 공방', '도예 체험'처럼 뒤에 말이 붙는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: I went to a pottery studio with a friend on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도예를 만들고 배우는 작업실을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for a workshop where people make and learn pottery.

phrases.en: I tried a pottery experience with my child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짧게 한번 해 보는 활동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a short, try-it-once activity.

phrases.en: My younger sibling majored in pottery at university.
phrases.nuance_ko: '도예'를 공부하는 분야로 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about pottery as a field of study.

explain_en: The art or craft of making ceramics, as a hobby or class (도예 수업) The finished item is '도자기' (ceramic ware), while the craft or field of making it is '도예'. It is often followed by another word, as in '도예 수업', '도예 공방' and '도예 체험'.
